set.st: Late May 1898: on the road back from Holy Hill, about 4 mi from Hartford, a man shot his companion, emptied his money bag (sworn at $1,028 in gold, silver, paper and change), dragged him down a slope and drove on to Hartford. He was arrested that night with $5.75; the bag and revolver were never found. Private farmland: permission. Pin is approximate, not the spot itself. Local papers of 1898-99 cover the shooting, the bail hearing and the conviction (one year and a $100 fine), and none reports the money recovered. A week after the shooting the Watertown Republican (8 Jun 1898) said 'the general opinion' was that the money was hidden by the assailant in the woods and the revolver thrown away; the Wisconsin Weekly Advocate (4 Jun 1898) also says 'no trace of the money' was found.

tw-wi-hartford-bauer-1898.t: The 1892 plats of Erin and Hartford show neither family, so the 1898 papers fix the road only as near Hartford toward Holy Hill.
src: Watertown Republican, 8 Jun 1898, p. 7, 'Money Hidden Away'
